Article Title: SIR row: 'Why does Gyanesh Kumar have lifelong immunity?' Rahul Gandhi asks, then answers
Article Text:
'PM Modi uses Gyanesh Kumar to steal elections': Rahul Gandhi on SIR irregularities

NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday questioned the legal immunity granted to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi uses him to “steal elections”.In a post on X, Gandhi wrote, “Q. Why is CEC Gyanesh Kumar the only Indian with lifelong blanket legal immunity? A. Because PM Modi uses him to steal elections.”This comes as top leaders of the INDIA bloc met in New Delhi on Wednesday to finalise an action plan for a joint agitation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with the Congress asserting that the opposition stands united to protect the Constitution from "repeated assaults" by the Modi government, including its alleged "vote chori gameplan" to remain in power.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former party chiefs Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, AICC general secretaries Jairam Ramesh and K C Venugopal, TMC chief Mamata Banerjee, and leaders of the SP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP(SP) and Shiv Sena (UBT), among others, attended the meeting."The INDIA janbandhan meeting just got underway. The parties participating are the Congress, Samajwadi Party, All India Trinamool Congress, NCP(SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), Rashtriya Janata Dal, CPI(M), CPI, Jammu and Kashmir National Conference, Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, CPI-ML, IUML, Kerala Congress (M), Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, RevolutionarySocialist Party, Kerala Congress (Jacob) and All India Forward Bloc," Ramesh said in a post on X."These and other Opposition parties stand united to protect the Constitution of India from repeated assaults of the Modi Government - most recently its Vote Chori gameplan through the ECI to remain in power," he added.Sources said a draft notice for a fresh motion seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha was ready and would be discussed at the meeting for approval.The DMK and AAP did not attend the meeting, while SP chief Akhilesh Yadav was also absent due to the Rajya Sabha nomination process in Uttar Pradesh.The meeting comes days after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on record at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), saying they had been issued without their knowledge or recommendation.Amid scrutiny over the concerns raised by the two Election Commissioners, the Election Commission said that differing views and observations were a normal part of deliberations in any institution. It also asserted that all its orders had full legal sanction and followed established statutory procedures.The last meeting of the INDIA bloc was held on June 8. Emphasising unity against the BJP, the alliance members had unanimously decided to seek the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-CBSE row and write to the Chief Justice of India on the SIR exercise and "vote loot".
Article Summary: Top leaders of the INDIA bloc met in New Delhi on Wednesday to finalise an action plan for a joint agitation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) The Congress asserting that the opposition stands united to protect the Constitution from "repeated assaults" by the Modi government.

Article Title: 'Divide Hindus for Muslim rule’: BJP invokes British ‘divide and rule’ policy to target Congress over Revanth Reddy remarks

What did Revanth Reddy say

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Wednesday drew a parallel between the British policy of “divide and rule” and what it described as the Congress ’ “divide Hindus for Muslim rule” approach, while targeting Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy over his remarks on Lord Ram and Lord Shiva.BJP MP and party spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi, speaking at a press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi, said, “The Britishers used the concept of divide and rule... Congress’ approach is to divide Hindus for Muslim rule.”To reinforce his argument, Trivedi claimed that Congress MP and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi had “deliberately chosen” a Muslim-majority constituency. He was referring to Rahul Gandhi’s former constituency of Wayanad in Keralam, a seat where Muslims account for more than 40% of the electorate and form the majority.The Congress leader currently represents Uttar Pradesh’s Raebareli constituency in the Lok Sabha.The controversy stems from Revanth Reddy’s remarks at a media conclave in New Delhi on September 28.Responding to a question about the Congress’ weak presence in North India, Reddy said, “We are Dravidians. People here (north) are Aryans. We are devotees of Shiva. These are devotees of Lord Ram. BJP stole Ram. It's an emotion.It's a sentiment. Why Modi ji does not say Har Har Mahadev. Have BJP people ever said Har Har Mahadev on a stage. They say only Jai Sri Ram. When we say Har Har Mahadev, they don't like it.”“Shiva is the God of the poor, Ram is the God of the rich and the BJP is a party of the rich,” he added.The remarks predictably drew a sharp response from the BJP, while the Congress defended Reddy, saying that Lord Ram “looks rich” and Lord Shiva “physically looks poor.”"Why should he (CM Revanth Reddy) apologise? I'm defending Revanth Reddy. Look-wise, Lord Ram wears a lot of ornaments. He looks rich, whereas Lord Shiva, with no clothes, physically looks poor. That is the difference. But we have affection for both the Gods, we pray to them, and we wish that both the Gods bless us," Telangana Congress president Mahesh Kumar Goud said.
Article Summary: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy made controversial remarks on Lord Ram and Lord Shiva. Reddy said, “We are Dravidians. People here (north) are Aryans. We are devotees of Shiva.” The remarks predictably drew a sharp response from the BJP, while the Congress defended Reddy.

NEW DELHI: Congress veteran Digvijaya Singh Tuesday told CWC that the political landscape would have been different if Nitish Kumar had been accommodated in 2023, referring to the JDU chief's then aspiration of becoming the convener of opposition INDIA bloc for Lok Sabha polls.Intending to stress that Congress should try to spread the opposition umbrella as BJP and RSS are on a weak footing, his argument was that if appeased, Kumar would not have defected to the BJP camp.As the remark triggered murmurs, members led by Kharge rebutted the claim saying Kumar was never interested. Article Title: Not just CEC, PM Modi and Shah should also resign for 'vote chori', says CWC
Article Text:
Referring to a meeting involving him, PM Modi and Shah, Rahul said the PM told him that after they lose, the Congress government will come in.

NEW DELHI: Raising the stakes in the ongoing controversy over special intensive revision (SIR) of poll rolls, the Congress Working Committee on Tuesday demanded that PM Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah resign on moral grounds, accusing them of being orchestrators of 'vote chori' through CEC Gyanesh Kumar. CWC, chaired by party chief Mallikarjun Kharge, also demanded the CEC's resignation, a halt to the SIR process, and restoration of over 13 crore voters deleted from the rolls.The meeting saw LoP Rahul Gandhi take the lead in arguing that the country now believes what the party and he had been saying for over two years: that the electoral rolls and EVMs were compromised by EC. He lamented that there were "non-believers" in Congress even when evidence was given about "vote chori".Referring to a meeting involving him, PM Modi and Shah, Rahul said the PM told him that after they lose, the Congress government will come in. Rahul had questioned how some appointments were being made despite his opposition, to which the PM had said Indira Gandhi also did that.Rahul said he had replied that Indira was voted out, after which PM Modi made the remark that Congress would follow BJP to office. Sources described the remark's context as Rahul's bid to rally non-believers within by mentioning that even the "BJP mascot" believes Congress will come to office.Rahul is learnt to have said the "big fishes" (PM Modi and Shah) know they are going to lose in future. He said that while there are questions about the 2014 and 2019 elections, the 2024 LS polls were unambiguously "match-fixed", and termed PM Modi as the "illegal PM". He repeatedly stressed "resistance" against the government.Putting Rahul's imprimatur on exposing "vote chori", the CWC resolution, read to the media by KC Venugopal and Jairam Ramesh, noted, "what began as one man's solitary warning is now a national demand for transparency and accountability".CWC stopped short of deciding an action plan, leaving it to the INDIA bloc, which will meet Wednesday.CWC meeting was attended by Sonia Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Sachin Pilot, Shashi Tharoor, Abhishek Singhvi, Manish Tewari, Randeep Singh Surjewala, Jitendra Singh, Prakash Joshi, CMs DK Shivakumar, Sukhwinder Sukhu, VD Satheesan, and Revanth Reddy, among others. Many CWC members and the four CMs are learnt to have argued that agitation in Delhi is important to having an impact.Kharge said, "Like in British times, Congress again has to shoulder the responsibility... we snatched the right to vote from the British and now fight to save that right."When Tharoor said the party should support the CJP agitation called on Oct 2, Kharge caustically asked the Keralam MP if he would be seen only in newspapers and on TV, or would join the street battle against the EC.
Article Summary: The Congress Working Committee on Tuesday demanded that PM Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah resign on moral grounds. CWC, chaired by party chief Mallikarjun Kharge, also demanded the CEC's resignation, a halt to the SIR process, and restoration of over 13 crore voters deleted from the rolls.

Article Title: Supreme Court to hear plea for CEC’s suspension, voiding SIR next week
Article Text:
Petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh alleged that about 14 decisions were taken in the EC’s name despite objections recorded by the two other election commissioners, S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear next week a petition filed against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, seeking his suspension and a declaration that the CEC cannot take unilateral decisions on the Election Commission ’s behalf.The petition also sought that special intensive revision of electoral rolls and all actions, decisions, directions and consequential measures undertaken pursuant to the exercise be declared void ab initio (invalid) and without lawful authority.The plea was mentioned by senior advocate Vikas Singh before CJI Surya Kant.Petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh alleged that about 14 decisions were taken in the EC’s name despite objections recorded by the two other election commissioners, S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.He sought a direction to the CEC to “show under what authority he has acted, and continues to act” as though he is individually entitled to exercise the collective decision-making power vested by Article 324 of the Constitution in the EC.Significantly, CEC has asserted that all decisions regarding SIR were taken unanimously by all election commissioners.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear next week a petition filed against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh alleged that about 14 decisions were taken in the EC’s name despite objections recorded by the two other election commissioners, S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

Article Title: BJP asks chief secy to ‘throw away’ statehood resolution, says it will strain Centre-J&K ties
Article Text:

SRINAGAR: A day after the Jammu & Kashmir assembly passed a resolution seeking restoration of statehood with a reference to autonomy, leader of opposition Sunil Sharma said the move would strain Centre-J&K relations and urged chief secretary Atal Dulloo not to forward the resolution to the Union govt. The BJP member also demanded speaker Abdul Rahim Rather’s resignation and claimed that Union home minister Amit Shah was unhappy about the resolution.“Already the chief secretary and the law secretary gave their opinion to the assembly that they cannot discuss the resolution as the issue is sub judice. Their communication to the assembly secretariat ahead of the resolution is an indication that the resolution is anti-Constitution. We expect the chief secretary not to forward the resolution to the Centre and throw it away,” Sharma told TOI.Sources said the assembly secretariat had sent the resolution to the chief secretary to be forwarded to the Centre.NC legislator Justice (retired) Hasnain Masoodi said the assembly secretariat should have directly sent it to the central govt instead of routing it through the chief secretary, as he had objected to the resolution.The assembly Monday adopted the resolution that seeks restoration of statehood amid protests and a walkout by BJP legislators, who accused NC and Congress of being anti-national over the reference to the autonomy resolution passed in the House in 2000.The chief secretary and the law secretary are facing criticism from the National Conference and other parties for writing to the assembly secretariat earlier, advising against taking up the resolution.Speaking in the House on Monday, CM Omar Abdullah, who moved the resolution, said he was also the law minister and was not even aware “that my law secretary is sending you opinions”.Sharma defended the two bureaucrats, saying they had expressed the “right opinion” as the resolution, he claimed, was “anti-constitutional” and “anti-national”.He said the speaker not only allowed the resolution to be introduced but also permitted amendments referring to autonomy and condemning the abrogation of Article 370, which was upheld by the Supreme Court. “The speaker has to step down,” he added. BJP has already moved a motion in the assembly against Rather.Sharma said the Centre was unhappy over the resolution as it would encourage separatism in J&K. “I met the (Union) home minister (Amit Shah) on Sunday. He expressed displeasure over the resolution,” Sharma said.According to Sharma, Shah told him during the meeting in New Delhi that statehood would be restored to J&K at an “appropriate time”, but anything that could disturb the peaceful situation would not be allowed.
Article Summary: Opposition leader Sunil Sharma urged chief secretary Atal Dulloo not to forward the resolution to the Union govt. He also demanded speaker Abdul Rahim Rather’s resignation and claimed that Union home minister Amit Shah was unhappy about the resolution.

Article Title: INDIA bloc meet: 'United' opposition to step up attack on EC, BJP - what's on agenda

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc is set to meet for the second time in four months on Wednesday to chalk out its response to the alleged differences within the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls.The opposition parties are likely to finalise a joint action plan, including an agitation against the EC's voter-roll exercise and a demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.The opposition will prepare a draft notice for a fresh bid to move a motion in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha for the removal of the CEC and deliberate on its approval at the meeting, sources told news agency PTI.On April 7, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairperson CP Radhakrishnan had rejected the opposition's first notice, which was signed by 130 Lok Sabha members and 63 Rajya Sabha members, seeking the CEC's removal over alleged partisanship and arbitrariness in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Meanwhile, a notice moved by 73 opposition MPs from Rajya Sabha on April 24 seeking Kumar's removal is already pending in the Upper House of Parliament.Article 324(5) of the Constitution states that the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office only "in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court."Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Congress parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi are expected to attend the opposition meeting.West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee are also expected to join. RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah and PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti are among the other leaders likely to participate.The Left parties are also expected to be represented, with CPM Rajya Sabha floor leader John Brittas likely to attend. Leaders of the CPI, CPI(ML), RSP and other Left parties are expected to join as well.Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray is likely to participate virtually due to prior engagements in Mumbai, including a campaign against the Election Commission.NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule and leaders of smaller opposition parties, including the JMM, IUML, VCK, MDMK, Kerala Congress factions, RLP, BAP, Lok Dal and Forward Bloc, are also expected to attend.Independent Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal is likely to participate in the deliberations.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav is unlikely to attend in person. The party is expected to send senior leaders instead. Reports said Akhilesh cited commitments linked to the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh and other prior engagements.The absence comes amid differences between the SP and Congress over seat-sharing discussions for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.The Aam Aadmi Party, DMK and Biju Janata Dal are among the parties that will not attend the meeting.The AAP was part of the INDIA bloc's 2024 Lok Sabha alliance but has since distanced itself from the grouping.The DMK, a Congress ally in Tamil Nadu, has also decided to stay away. DMK spokesperson TKS Elangovan said the party remained aligned with the opposition on several issues but was no longer part of the INDIA bloc. He said the party would support a removal motion against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar if one is brought in Parliament.BJD will also skip the meeting.The meeting comes amid the opposition's campaign against the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.This comes after a report revealed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on record at least 14 times in the past 10 months over SIR-related decisions and orders they said were issued without their knowledge or recommendation.The EC has rejected suggestions of institutional dysfunction, saying differing views are a normal part of deliberations and that its orders have full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.The opposition has sought to use the SIR controversy to press its demands against the poll panel and the government, while attempting to bring different opposition parties together.The previous INDIA bloc meeting was held on June 8. The parties had then decided to demand the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-CBSE row and write to the Chief Justice of India over the SIR exercise and allegations of "vote loot".
Article Summary: Opposition parties likely to finalise a joint action plan, including an agitation against the EC's voter-roll exercise and a demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Opposition will prepare a draft notice for a fresh bid to move a motion in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha for the removal of the CEC.

Article Title: Nandigram: Calcutta HC grants interim bail to Congress candidate Milan Pradhan to contest bypoll
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Calcutta high court on Tuesday granted interim bail to Congress candidate Milan Pradhan to contest the Nandigram bypoll, bar and bench reported.Pradhan was sent to judicial custody until October 7 by a court in West Bengal’s Purba Medinipur district on Wednesday, in connection with the case. The Additional chief judicial Magistrate of Contai Court had rejected his bail plea after the prosecution sought his custody on murder charges.Pradhan was already in judicial custody until October 5 in a separate Arms Act case. His lawyer, Prasenjit Jana, said he was arraigned on murder and other charges in connection with a case registered during the 2007 Nandigram anti-land acquisition movement.The high court had agreed to hear the Congress candidate’s bail plea on Thursday after the party moved it against his arrest. The development came after Justice Sauagata Bhattacharyya verbally asked the state government on Tuesday to allow Pradhan to contest the bypoll, provided he secured bail in the five criminal cases in which he had been arrested.Pradhan was arrested on September 18, hours after West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee announced that her faction of the Trinamool Congress would support him in Nandigram. The party’s candidate, Sanchita Pradhan De, had withdrawn from the contest.The following day, Pradhan was sent to judicial custody until October 3 by the Haldia sub-divisional court in connection with four other pending non-bailable arrest warrants linked to cases dating back to 2007.Several criminal cases were registered against Pradhan in 2007 at police stations in Nandigram and Khejuri in Purba Medinipur district.During a hearing on his plea seeking protection from coercive action in six other cases, the state government told the high court on Tuesday that five cases had been withdrawn by the previous government and that Pradhan was not wanted in the sixth.The court was also informed that he had been arrested and remanded to judicial custody in connection with the other five cases.The Nandigram bypoll is scheduled for October 6, with campaigning set to conclude on October 4. Counting of votes will take place on October 9.The bypoll was necessitated after chief minister Suvendu Adhikari vacated Nandigram and retained Bhabanipur, from where he had won in the Assembly elections held earlier this year. He had won both seats. The BJP formed its first government in West Bengal, ending the Trinamool Congress’s 15-year rule.
Article Summary: Pradhan was already in judicial custody until October 5 in a separate Arms Act case. His lawyer, Prasenjit Jana, said he was arraigned on murder and other charges in connection with a case registered during the 2007 Nandigram anti-land acquisition movement.

Article Title: Revanth Reddy's Ram-Shiva remarks: Congress defends Telangana CM as BJP demands apology
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday defended Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy for drawing a contrast between Lord Ram and Shiva, saying that the remarks were directed against Bharatiya Janata Party which is doing politics "in the name of Lord Ram."Congress Telangana chief Mahesh Kumar Goud said that BJP is trying to own Lord Ram and fetch votes in the elections and said that it is not a good practice."What Revanth Reddy has said is that Lord Ram looks rich because of his clothing, while Lord Shiva looks very poor. Physically, when we see both the Gods, one feels that Shiva represents the poor and Lord Ram represents the rich. But both the Gods are the same to us, and we pray to both the Gods. But unfortunately, the BJP is doing politics in the name of Lord Ram. The BJP is trying to own Ram and fetch votes in the elections. This is not a good practice," Goud said."Why should he (CM Revanth Reddy) apologise? I'm defending Revanth Reddy. Look-wise, Lord Ram wears a lot of ornaments. He looks rich, whereas Lord Shiva, with no clothes, physically looks poor. That is the difference. But we have affection for both the Gods, we pray to them, and we wish that both the Gods bless us," he added.This comes after Reddy on September 28 claimed that Congress had succeeded only in the southern states but struggled in the north because the BJP had "stolen Lord Ram", who is revered there, while Lord Shiva is worshipped in the south.Speaking at an interactive session organised by a media organisation in Delhi, Reddy also claimed that Shiva was the God of the poor, Ram was the God of the rich, and the BJP was a party of the rich.Meanwhile, Reddy's remarks strong response from Union minister Sanjay Kumar Bandi, who accused the Telangana chief minister of creating political divisions between Lord Ram and Lord Shiva.In a post on X, Bandi said Reddy, who had earlier remarked that “Muslim is Congress, Congress is Muslim”, was now “drawing political boundaries between Lord Ram & Lord Shiva”."Being the CM of Telangana that has Dakshina Kashi at Vemulawada and Dakshina Ayodhya at Bhadrachalam, Revanth Reddy should know better than to divide Lord Rama and Lord Shiva into North and South," he said.Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao also criticised Reddyand said, "Revanth Reddy's statement with regard to Ram and Shiv and comparing that Ram belongs to the rich and Shiv belongs to the poor, and PM Modi always says 'Jai Shri Ram' but doesn't say 'Har Har Mahadev' is an absurd and insulting statement to the Hindu religion. In fact, it is a statement given with an intention to break the Hindu community.""Of late, Revanth Reddy has converted himself into 'Revanthuddin' because he says that Muslim is Congress and Congress is Muslim. So perhaps he must be feeling that he's still a Muslim and therefore trying to divide the Hindu community," he added.
Article Summary: Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy drew a contrast between Lord Ram and Shiva. Reddy said that Ram looks rich because of his clothing, while Shiva looks very poor. Union minister Sanjay Kumar Bandi accused Reddy of creating political divisions.

Article Title: 12 BJP CMs defend EC amid SIR row, hit back at Rahul Gandhi after poll body's fresh note
Article Text:

The controversy

NEW DELHI: A dozen BJP chief ministers held press conferences in their respective states on Sunday, a day after the Election Commission of India (ECI) issued a press release responding to a media report that had claimed a “rift” between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.According to a statement issued by the ruling party, the chief ministers accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and his party-led opposition INDIA bloc of “conspiring to defame constitutional institutions."In states where the BJP or its NDA allies are not in power, state BJP presidents or leaders of the opposition from the saffron party addressed media instead.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis remarked that "no vote was stolen, Rahul Gandhi's mind was stolen." He accused the Lok Sabha leader of opposition of "seeking to spread anarchy by defaming institutions" while claiming to defend the Constitution.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath accused the opposition parties of creating "confusion" over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. In Assam, Himanta Biswa Sarma described the INDIA bloc as an “alliance of losers,” while Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary argued that "cleansing" the voter list was necessary because “booth capturing no longer works in the country.”West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari pointed to the Congress’s support for the SIR in Keralam, where it won, and its opposition to the exercise in Bengal after losing the election.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami objected to what he described as an "attempt to defame institutions by presenting a note from an internal discussion as a final decision.”Rajasthan chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma questioned why the Congress had not "verified the facts" before making serious allegations over the June 24, 2025, orders concerning the nationwide SIR, which he maintained were adopted by the ECI full consensus of the CEC and the election commissioners.Chhattisgarh's Vishnu Deo Sai accused the Congress of resorting to “anti-national” conduct after “having lost more than 100 elections.” Referring to the Election Commissioners’ joint statement, accompanied by a photograph of the three officials seated at a table, Sai argued that it had exposed what he called a “conspiracy to tarnish the country’s image.”Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, where a third of the electorate was removed and a third of those remaining received notices as part of the ongoing revision, framed the Opposition’s position on the issue as an attempt to “divert attention from its failures."Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, posted cryptically on X: “I love swimming in the sea when it’s rough. It teaches you that rough is just another kind of calm.”At a press conference on September 24, a day after The Indian Express published its report, the Congress leader claimed his “vote chori” (vote theft) allegation stood “vindicated.” The Raebareli MP also demanded that CEC Gyanesh Kumar resign or be removed, accusing him of “treason.”The Indian Express reported on September 23 that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected to at least 14 decisions over 10 months concerning the ongoing SIR exercise and related matters.The ECI has not disputed that objections were raised; however it characterised them as "disagreements" that were subsequently resolved, stressing that the final decisions were "unanimous." While Sandhu and Joshi are yet to speak to the media, the poll panel's press note second statement outlined several measures and clarifications.The BJP has maintained that the ECI’s press notes have “settled the matter”. Its allies, who, like the opposition, had sought an explanation from the poll body, also welcomed the commission's statement.
Article Summary: A dozen BJP chief ministers held press conferences in their respective states on Sunday. The chief ministers accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and his party-led opposition INDIA bloc of “conspiring to defame constitutional institutions” In states where the BJP or its NDA allies are not in power, state BJP presidents or leaders of the opposition from the saffron party addressed media instead.

Article Title: DU college sets up panel to probe poll ‘malpractices’
Article Text:
The two have asked how many NOTA votes were cast and asked for the unedited CCTV footage of polling day too.





NEW DELHI: Aditi Mahavidyalaya, a DU college, has formed a committee to investigate allegations of irregularities in its college-level elections after two candidates alleged discrepancies in counting, EVM handling and said that non-students, including a BJP functionary, were near a booth on the polling day.All the candidates who won the election on Sept 18 were backed by ABVP.On Sept 21, Diya Chhabra, who contested for president, and Prachi Wadhwa, who contested for secretary, sent a representation to the college, alleging election malpractice. The college informed them on Sept 24 that it had formed a probe committee.According to a result sheet that Chhabra and Wadhwa have submitted, 568 votes were cast across the two booths — 315 in booth 1 and 253 in booth 2. However, the number of votes recorded for the posts varied. For president, the total was 563 -- 314 in booth 1 and 249 in 2. For secretary, the votes cast were 539 -- 311 in booth 1 and 228 in booth 2. For the joint secretary post, 542 votes were cast -- the booth-wise break-up was 311 and 231.The duo said that while the shortfall was between one and four votes for president, the shortfall was 25 votes for secretary and 22 for joint secretary in booth 2.The two have asked how many NOTA votes were cast and asked for the unedited CCTV footage of polling day too.They also alleged that an observer in booth 1 was not allowed to stay inside the polling area and that EVMs were opened before voting without a verification by the candidates. A non-student, that too a man, was allowed on the women’s college campus during the campaign and the polling and was seen near a booth on Sept 18 between 11.30am and 1pm with BJP MLA Ravinder Indraj Singh, they wrote.When Singh was asked about this, he said that as a “public representative” he had gone to the campus. "The college is in my constituency, and I had got complaints about some commotion there.”The duo has approached Delhi High Court. “It is troubling that a college is alleged to have manipulated vote counts and allowed external political functionaries in,” counsel Shaurya Vikram said.Calls and texts to principal Neelam Rathi went unanswered.
Article Summary: Aditi Mahavidyalaya, a DU college, has formed a committee to investigate allegations of irregularities. Two candidates alleged discrepancies in counting, EVM handling and said that non-students, including a BJP functionary, were near a booth on the polling day.

Article Title: Hyderabad shocker: Man kills wife with pestle after dispute, surrenders before police
Article Text:
Narender, a 25-year-old man, reportedly killed his wife Teja Sri at their home in Baglingampalli





HYDERABAD: A 25-year-old man allegedly killed his wife by attacking her with a pestle at their residence in Baglingampalli on Sunday. The accused was identified as Narender, an accountant at a hotel in RTC Crossroads.According to police officials, Narender married Teja Sri about five years ago. However, their relationship had become strained. On Sunday, the couple had an argument, following which Narender, allegedly in a fit of rage, attacked Teja Sri on the head with a pestle. She died on the spot. Later, Narender went to the police station and surrendered.Police reached the spot and shifted the body to Gandhi Hospital for postmortem. Forensic experts were called to the scene to collect evidence. Police registered a murder case against Narender.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old man allegedly killed his wife by attacking her with a pestle at their residence in Baglingampalli on Sunday. The accused was identified as Narender, an accountant at a hotel in RTC Crossroads. According to police officials, Narender married Teja Sri about five years ago.

Article Title: Gulzar Singh case: Complainant has no video of father’s death, cops tell Punjab and Haryana high court
Article Text:
The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.





CHANDIGARH: Punjab govt has told the Punjab and Haryana high court that despite repeated efforts, the original video/device on which alleged suicide victim Gulzar Singh’s purported video was recorded has not been handed over to the police by the complainant or his family members.In its status report filed before the division bench of Chief Justice Ashwini Kumar and Justice Rohit Kapoor, the state govt said efforts were made to bring on record the original video/device, but the complainant and the family members of Gulzar Singh did not submit them.The report states that notices under Section 94 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were issued to complainant Lakhwinder Singh, who is Gulzar’s son, on Sept 15, 17, 20 and 27 for the production of the device. The report stated that Lakhwinder, in his statement on Sept 27, stated that he did not have any video regarding the death of his father.The SIT, however, said multiple videos had been collected as part of the investigation through social-media monitoring. “The said videos have been obtained through social monitoring vide DDR No. 45 dated September 26, 2026,” the report states.It states that the videos are being analysed as “there are multiple videos with different versions”.According to the status report, in one of the videos, Gulzar Singh is heard naming Raj Sarpanch, Vicky, Sukha Conductor and Gona, who are accused in the present FIR. The report states that “his statement in the said video corroborates with the statement given by complainant Lakhwinder Singh”.The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.The police said notices were also issued under Section 94 of the BNSS to media channels, calling upon them to provide the original video recordings along with requisite certificates under Section 63(4)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, “for the purpose of establishing their authenticity”.The status report has been filed by Sangrur senior superintendent of police Dr Rajvot Grewal, a member of the special investigation team that is probing the suicide case, in compliance with the high court’s Sept 16 order.The report states that FIR No. 204 dated Sept 8 was registered at Dirba police station under Section 108 of the BNS and sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against five persons — Baljit Singh alias Raj, Sukhdev Singh alias Sukha Conductor, Vicky Singh alias Vicky Member, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur.It states that Baljit, Vicky, Gona and Baljinder were arrested on Sept 8 and remanded in judicial custody. Sukhdev, however, “is absconding as on today”.Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the local drug menace on Sept 6.The SIT said a look-out circular was issued against Sukhdev, besides a message to all SHOs in Punjab, a public notice and letters to the Regional Transport Authority, Lead Bank, Sangrur, and Bureau of Immigration to trace him and gather information about his vehicle, financial transactions and travel history. Multiple raids were also conducted at his residence, relatives houses and other possible locations.A petition was filed before the Punjab and Haryana high court seeking transfer of the investigation to the CBI or another independent agency, alleging that Gulzar Singh had faced intimidation and that his video statement contained allegations against certain persons.
Article Summary: Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema.

Article Title: Watch: Truck carrying fish overturns, spills load across Delhi-Meerut Expressway; car crashes into it
Article Text:
A truck transporting fish overturned on the Delhi-Meerut Expressway after its front tyre burst, causing an accident (Visuals credit: X)





GHAZIABAD: A fish-laden truck overturned on Delhi-Meerut Expressway in Ghaziabad after its front tyre burst around 9am on Wednesday, causing an Alto car travelling behind it to crash into the vehicle.No injuries were reported.Kavi Nagar police station SHO Anurag Sharma said the truck was travelling from Delhi to Meerut when the driver lost control after the tyre burst.The truck first hit the divider and then overturned, scattering fish across the expressway.The Alto car, which was also heading towards Meerut, subsequently crashed into the truck.Police rescued the truck driver and his helper. They and the occupant of the Alto car were stable, Sharma said.Both vehicles were moved to the nearest police chowki.Police collected the fish in a container and guarded them to prevent looting.
Article Summary: Fish-laden truck overturned on Delhi-Meerut Expressway in Ghaziabad. Front tyre of truck burst around 9am on Wednesday, causing an Alto car to crash into it. No injuries were reported. Police collected the fish in a container and guarded them to prevent looting.

Article Title: ‘Wait and face criticism’: Audio clip of Ashok Chavan fuels row over Mudkhed, Mukhed exclusion from drought list
Article Text:
​Rajya Sabha member Ashok Chavan (second from right) along with his daughter and Bhokar BJP MLA Sreejaya on Monday submitted a memorandum to revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, regarding inclusion of Mudkhed and Mukhed talukas in the list of drought-affected talukas

​Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





An alleged audio call between BJP MP Ashok Chavan and a party worker has gone viral, escalating the political row over Mudkhed and Mukhed talukas being left out of state govt’s drought-relief list.In the audio clip, a party worker was allegedly heard confronting former CM Chavan over the omission of Mudkhed from the drought list, saying residents were angry and demanding answers. In the clip, the worker reportedly told Chavan that BJP cadre were facing sharp criticism from farmers and citizens who believed the region was facing drought-like conditions despite being left out of the notified list.Responding to the concerns, Chavan could be heard urging restraint, saying less than 24 hours had elapsed since govt’s announcement. He allegedly advised the worker against launching protests and assured him that Mudkhed would eventually be included in the drought list.At one stage, Chavan was purportedly heard telling the worker to “remain calm and face the criticism”, while asking party workers to trust the process and wait for further developments. The worker, however, continued to question why Mudkhed and Mukhed were excluded when almost the entire state, including most of Marathwada, received drought recognition.The audio has rapidly circulated across social media platforms, amplifying discontent among farmers and residents of the two Nanded district talukas.The controversy stems from Maharashtra govt’s decision to declare drought-like conditions in 265 of the state’s 358 talukas following deficient rainfall. In Marathwada, 74 of 76 talukas were included, with Mukhed and Mudkhed emerging as the only exceptions.The issue carries added political significance as Mudkhed tehsil falls within Bhokar assembly constituency, represented by Chavan’s daughter and first-time BJP MLA Sreejaya Chavan. Mukhed assembly constituency is represented by BJP MLA Tushar Rathod, who is serving his third consecutive term.Officials have maintained that both talukas had failed to meet the trigger-I criteria under the state’s drought assessment framework. Nanded collector Rahul Kardile, however, said Mudkhed and Mukhed would be reassessed under the next evaluation trigger scheduled for early Oct.Chavan has separately sought the inclusion of both talukas, arguing that technical rainfall data does not adequately capture the extent of crop losses caused by prolonged dry spells. He has maintained that ground realities and agricultural damage in the two regions warrant their inclusion in the drought-relief list.
Article Summary: Mudkhed and Mukhed talukas were left out of state govt’s drought-relief list. An alleged audio call between BJP MP Ashok Chavan and a party worker has gone viral. The audio has rapidly circulated across social media platforms.

Article Title: Farmer dies after consuming poison; wife alleges harassment over Rs 9 lakh loan; abetment case against moneylender
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





A Rs 9 lakh loan cost a Kolhapur farmer Rs 25 lakh, and ultimately, his life, his wife said, accusing a private moneylender of harassment. Police have booked the private moneylender for abetment to suicide, though his whereabouts are currently unknown.Police said 48-year-old Shridhar Davare, a resident of Sonage village in Kagal, died on Saturday after allegedly consuming weedicide on Sept 23. Police found two notes in Davare’s pockets, which are suspected to be dying declarations. In a text message to his wife, Savita, before taking the extreme step, Davare asked her to look after their son, she told police.Davare was first taken to a private hospital in Nipani. As his condition deteriorated, he was shifted to CPR Hospital in Kolhapur, where he died on Saturday.Following his death, Savita lodged a complaint against the private moneylender. She alleged that her husband had borrowed Rs 9 lakh from him and repaid a total of Rs 25 lakh over the past five years. Despite this, she alleged, the lender continued demanding more money, claiming that the loan and interest had not been fully repaid. She also accused him of harassing and physically assaulting Davare over the dues.Police have registered a case under BNS sections 108, 115(2) and 351(1), along with sections 39 and 45 of the Maharashtra Money-Lending (Regulation) Act, 2014.
Article Summary: Shridhar Davare, 48, died on Saturday after allegedly consuming weedicide. Police found two notes in Davare’s pockets, which are suspected to be dying declarations. Police have booked the private moneylender for abetment to suicide, though his whereabouts are currently unknown.

Article Title: Cops on Ganpati patrol hit by speeding MUV on Thane-Belapur Road, driver flees
Article Text:
The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a hit-and-run incident on the Thane-Belapur Road, a police constable and a woman assistant sub-inspector (ASI) were injured when a speeding MUV rammed into their motorcycle from behind while they were patrolling during the seventh day of Ganpati immersion.The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday.The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, who was riding his personal motorcycle, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion.The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV. Patil sustained injuries to his left leg, while Magar suffered bruises to her left elbow, shoulder and left leg.Acting on a complaint filed by Patil, Rabale MIDC police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Motor Vehicles Act against the MUV driver. Police traced him to his residence in Ghansoli.Devidas Kathale, senior inspector of Rabale MIDC police, said, “As the accused MUV driver's wife is due to deliver in a few days, he will be summoned to the police station later and served with a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.”
Article Summary: The incident took place near Digha pond on the Belapur-bound lane at around 12.20am on Monday. The injured cops were identified as constable Umesh Patil, 41, and ASI Rashmin Magar, who was riding pillion. The motorcycle skidded after being hit by the MUV.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Father, lawyer seek police protection, allege threats from Sena (UBT) leaders
Article Text:
Ojha questioned Aaditya Thackeray’s ‘Y-plus’ security, saying those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

(With agency inputs)





THANE: Advocate Nilesh Ojha on Sunday said that Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection, alleging that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Ojha, who is representing Satish Salian in the case, said they have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Chief Justice of India and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, seeking protection."The CBI FIR was registered, and a letter was immediately written requesting police protection for four individuals: Satish Salian, our witness Sameer Wankhede, myself, and Ashutosh Pathak, " Ojha told news agency ANI.Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray , saying those who brought the matter to light and allegedly faced threats had been left without protection."The letter clearly states, citing records from your Home Ministry and the Narcotics Bureau, that it is evident that Aditya Thackeray is involved in the drug trade. Furthermore, an FIR has now been registered against him regarding gang rape, murder, and a cover-up.Several other high-profile individuals and police officers are also implicated as accused in this matter," he said."We have already provided all prima facie evidence; the CBI has obtained everything necessary during the investigation to secure a conviction. Yet, the accused currently enjoys 'Y-plus' security provided by your administration. Meanwhile, those who brought this matter to light and those facing direct threats from individuals like Sanjay Raut were left unprotected," the advocate added.He further said that providing security was mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines, and alleged that their request for protection had not been acted upon.He further added, "Providing security is mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines. Yet, they failed to do so. Consequently, we compiled all the material and handed it over to the CBI. We also urged them to investigate the role of Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and determine why police protection was not granted.""We have given a copy of this to the CBI, along with Prime Minister Modi ji, the Home Minister, the Chief Justice of India, and the Chief Minister," Ojha said.Disha Salian was found dead in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Her death was initially registered as an Accidental Death Report (ADR).Salian died days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput , whose death also led to a high-profile investigation and widespread public controversy.Bombay High Court directed the CBI to register a formal First Information Report (FIR) and launch a fresh probe.As the probe progresses, Satish Salian, accompanied by his lawyer Nilesh Ojha, has submitted a pen drive containing material they described as evidence related to Disha Salian’s death.Meanwhile, Aaditya Thackeray has denied the allegations and responded to the defamation notice issued by Satish Salian.
Article Summary: Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection. They allege that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders. Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray. He said those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

Article Title: PM classmate’s battle for land continues despite BJP MLA's exit, no possession yet
Article Text:
Asgar Ali Vora met the PM on Sept 8 and sought his intervention in the land disp­u­te





BHAYANDAR: Asgar Ali Vora, a schoolmate of Prime Minister Narendra Modi , continues to struggle to regain possession of his land after MLA Narendra Mehta’s company announced that it had relinquished the property. However, another developer is allegedly continuing to retain possession of the land.Vora, 81, had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayandar East in 1989. He has alleged that Swayam Builders and Mehta’s Seven Eleven Constructions took possession of the property in 2011. After pursuing the matter for nearly 15 years, Vora met PM Modi on Sep 8 and complained against Mehta.Following the meeting, Mehta relinquished possession of the land, while the municipal corporation also cancelled the construction permission granted to him.However, the land has allegedly not been handed back to its original owner. Instead, developers Mukesh Parekh and Mervyn Fernandes are allegedly continuing to retain possession of the property. Following a complaint by Shiv Sena, Navghar police have registered a non-cognisable offence against Seven Eleven Constructions, Parekh and Fernandes.
Article Summary: Asgar Ali Vora, 81, had purchased around 2,810 sq m of land at Navghar in Bhayandar East in 1989. He has alleged that Swayam Builders and Mehta’s Seven Eleven Constructions took possession of the property in 2011. After pursuing the matter for nearly 15 years, Vora met PM Modi on Sep 8 and complained.

Article Title: Woman dies by suicide at her Dhanori residence
Article Text:
Pune:





A 25-year-old woman died by suicide in her Munjaba Vasti flat in Dhanori after alleged physical and verbal assault by her boyfriend (32) on Sept 22. Vishrantwadi police registered a case of abetment against the boyfriend on Monday on a complaint by her brother.Police said the deceased woman had been living with her boyfriend for the past two years after she broke away from her marriage. The boyfriend allegedly used to harass and abuse her in an inebriated state, accusing her of infidelity.On Sept 22, when her partner was out and she did not answer the door or receive calls, neighbours called up officials. Police and city fire brigade officials broke into the flat and found her body. She was taken to Sassoon hospital only to be declared dead on arrival.The police complaint states that her boyfriend had sold off all her gold jewellery to buy a two-wheeler for himself.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old woman died by suicide in her Munjaba Vasti flat in Dhanori on Sept 22. Vishrantwadi police registered a case of abetment against the boyfriend on a complaint by her brother. The deceased woman had been living with her boyfriend for the past two years after she broke away from her marriage.

Article Title: CM Vijay’s visit: Traffic diversions announced in Coimbatore
Article Text: COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore city police have announced temporary traffic diversions on arterial roads in view of the visit of chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Wednesday. The CM will arrive here en route to Dharapuram, where he will be campaigning for P Sathyabama who is the TVK candidate for the Oct 6 byelection.Buses entering Coimbatore city from Salem, Erode and Tirupur are restricted from passing through Neelambur, Chinniyampalayam and the airport on the Avinashi Road. Instead, these vehicles must divert at Neelambur and take L&T Bypass via Chinthamanipudur, Ondipudur and Singanallur to enter the city. Light vehicles from the Neelambur side are also advised to go via L&T Bypass, Chinthamanipudur, Ondipudur and Singanallur to reach the city.Vehicles exiting the city via the Avinashi Road must make a U-turn at Lakshmi Mills Junction and proceed via Puliyakulam, Ramanathapuram and Singanallur to reach L&T Bypass.Light motor vehicles exiting via the Avinashi Road and the V K Road should take a diversion through the Masakalipalayam Road to reach Singanallur. Vehicles arriving via Avinashi Road / Hope College Junction must make a U-turn at Tidel Park Junction and proceed via the Kamarajar Road to Singanallur.Heavy vehicles heading towards the Avinashi Road from Kalapatti Junction must divert at Kalapatti Junction and proceed via Thennampalayam.Heavy vehicles approaching the Avinashi Road from the Goldwins Road should turn right at the Housing Unit Road / Maruti Bakery Junction and proceed via the Veeriyampalayam Road to reach Kalapatti Junction.Passengers are advised to reach the airport at least 30 minutes prior to their scheduled travel time. Parking for call taxis and private vehicles on the airport premises will not be permitted.Entry of trucks into the city is prohibited between 7am and 9pm on Wednesday.Trucks travelling from Walayar towards Salem on the Kochi - Salem National Highway are advised to take the alternative route via Palathurai Junction and Karpagam College Junction towards Othakkalmandapam, Chettipalayam, Pappampatti, Selakarichal and Karadivavi. Trucks going towards Walayar are advised to travel to Sulur via Chinthamanipudur and Pappampatti. Trucks travelling from Annur towards Avinashi and Karumathampatti are prohibited from passing through Somanur.
Article Summary: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay will arrive in Coimbatore on Wednesday. Buses entering city from Salem, Erode and Tirupur are restricted from passing through Neelambur, Chinniyampalayam and the airport on the Avinashi Road.

Article Title: Two held with 189kg gutka, 500g ganja in Coimbatore
Article Text:
The seizure was made during a vehicle check in Vadavalli on Sunday

Coimbatore:





City police seized 189kg of gutka products and 500g of ganja from a taxi during a vehicle check near Vadavalli on Sunday and arrested two men in connection with the seizure. Police also seized the car in which the contraband was found.The arrested have been identified as B Andrews, 41, of Madukkarai, and R Selva, 28, from Sivaganga district. They were apprehended when police conducted a vehicle check following a tip-off.The two were subsequently produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody. Police are investigating the source of the contraband and the intended recipients as part of the probe.
Article Summary: City police seized 189kg of gutka products and 500g of ganja from a taxi during a vehicle check near Vadavalli. Police also seized the car in which the contraband was found. The arrested have been identified as B Andrews, 41, of Madukkarai, and R Selva, 28, from Sivaganga district.

Article Title: Woman cop dies after chasing assault suspect in Paramakudi
Article Text:
head constable kannagi (file picture)

Ramanathapuram

:





A woman head constable collapsed and died while chasing a 25-year-old man who allegedly assaulted another person in the emergency ward of the Paramakudi govt hospital on Monday. Police arrested the man on Tuesday in connection with the incident.Police said M Kannagi, a woman head constable, was on duty at the police assistance centre in the emergency ward of the hospital around 8pm on Monday when she witnessed a man slap another person.Kannagi immediately attempted to apprehend the alleged assailant. The man allegedly pushed her aside and tried to flee. Undeterred, Kannagi chased him for about 50m, but he managed to escape from the hospital premises.Police said Kannagi subsequently returned to the emergency ward and went to the dressing room, where she suddenly fainted. Nurses rushed her to doctors, who administered CPR and made efforts to revive her. However, she died despite treatment.Paramakudi Town police registered a case and launched a search for the man who had fled the hospital.Following an investigation, police arrested the suspect, identified as Karuvayan alias Karuppuraja, of Kumarakurichi in Sivaganga district, on Tuesday morning.Chief minister C Joseph Vijay offered his condolences and announced Rs30 lakh for the family of the bereaved.
Article Summary: M Kannagi, a woman head constable, was on duty at the police assistance centre in the emergency ward of the Paramakudi govt hospital on Monday. She witnessed a man slap another person and attempted to apprehend the alleged assailant. The man allegedly pushed her aside and tried to flee. Police arrested the man on Tuesday in connection with the incident.

Article Title: Wayanad man on the run for minor’s sexual assault arrested
Article Text:
Vaisakh

Idukki

:





A man who allegedly sexually assaulted a minor girl after befriending her through Instagram and promising to marry her was arrested after absconding during the trial of the case. The accused, Vaishakh, a native of Pozhuthana in Wayanad, was arrested by members of the Idukki district police chief’s long pending (LP) Squad.According to police, the incident took place in 2024. The accused allegedly entered the girl’s house and sexually assaulted her after promising marriage. He went into hiding during the trial proceedings.The LP squad traced and arrested him from Njarakkal in Ernakulam. Vaishakh was subsequently handed over to the Kanjikuzhi police for further legal proceedings.
Article Summary: The accused, Vaishakh, a native of Pozhuthana in Wayanad, was arrested by members of the Idukki district police chief’s long pending (LP) Squad. The incident took place in 2024. The accused allegedly entered the girl's house and sexually assaulted her after promising marriage.

Article Title: Elderly woman killed by husband in Kothamangalam
Article Text:
Kochi

:





An elderly woman was allegedly killed by her husband at their residence in Happy Nagar, Kothamangalam, around 2am on Tuesday. The deceased was Kunjamma (62).According to the FIR registered by the Kothamangalam police, Kuriakose P V, 67, allegedly stabbed his wife with a knife following a dispute. After the autopsy, the mortal remains were handed over to the relatives. Police said further investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the alleged attack.

Article Title: Kerala HC seeks details of steps taken to conduct socio-economic caste survey in state
Article Text:
Outside view of the High Court complex in Kochi

Kochi

:





The HC has directed the state govt to file an affidavit disclosing the steps taken so far to conduct a socio-economic caste survey.A bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V M Syam Kumar issued the order in a contempt case filed by the Minority Indians Planning and Vigilance Commission Trust alleging non-compliance with an earlier order in a petition relating to the inadequate representation of backward classes in two public services and the state govt’s failure to conduct a socio-economic survey in terms of the Kerala State Backward Classes Act. The court directed backward classes development department secretary Veena N Madhavan to file the affidavit within four weeks.Earlier, the director of the department had appeared in person and stated that, as the head of the directorate, he was entrusted with implementing schemes and programmes formulated by the govt for the educational, social and related upliftment of backward classes. He further stated that the director had no independent authority to order such a survey, decide on the use of Socio-Economic and Caste Census - 2011 data or revise the state list. Accordingly, the bench suo motu impleaded Madhavan as an additional respondent and directed her to file an affidavit.During the hearing, the petitioner’s counsel referred to a govt order issued by the Telangana govt and stated that it had undertaken a comprehensive door-to-door household survey covering socio-economic, educational, employment, political and caste aspects. The survey was intended to plan and implement opportunities for the amelioration of Backward Classes, SC and ST citizens and other weaker sections. Accordingly, the bench asked the additional advocate general to examine the Telangana govt’s order and, if necessary, consider whether a similar order was required to implement the directions issued by the court. The matter was adjourned to Nov 5.
Article Summary: HC has directed the state govt to file an affidavit disclosing the steps taken so far to conduct a socio-economic caste survey. A bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V M Syam Kumar issued the order in a contempt case filed by the Minority Indians Planning and Vigilance Commission Trust.
